member.name: M:MelloSilveiraTools.MechanicsOfMaterials.Fatigue.FatigueCalculator.CalculateSurfaceFactor(System.Double,MelloSilveiraTools.MechanicsOfMaterials.Models.Enums.SurfaceFinish)
member.summary: Calculates the Marin surface factor k_a using the empirical correlation k_a = a · S_ut^b, where the (a, b) pair is selected from the surface finish (rectified, machined/cold-rolled, hot-rolled or as-forged/wrought). Reference: Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, Table 6-2.
member.param: The ultimate tensile strength S_ut of the material, in MPa.
The manufacturing surface finish of the part.
member.returns: The dimensionless surface factor k_a.

member.name: M:MelloSilveiraTools.MechanicsOfMaterials.Fatigue.FatigueCalculator.CalculateSizeFactor(MelloSilveiraTools.MechanicsOfMaterials.Models.Profiles.Profile,MelloSilveiraTools.MechanicsOfMaterials.Models.Fatigue.LoadingType,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Calculates the Marin size factor k_b. Returns 1 for purely axial loading. For bending or torsion the factor depends on the equivalent diameter d_e of the cross-section: for circular sections d_e = D when the section rotates about its axis or 0.37·D otherwise; for rectangular sections d_e = h when rotating or 0.808·√(b·h) otherwise. The piecewise correlation comes from Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design (k_b = (d_e/7.62)^-0.107 for 2.79 ≤ d_e ≤ 51 mm and k_b = 1.51·d_e^-0.157 for 51 < d_e ≤ 254 mm).
member.param: The cross-section profile (circular or rectangular). Linear dimensions are expected in millimeters.
The loading type applied to the part.
True when the section rotates relative to the load direction (e.g. a rotating shaft); false otherwise.
member.returns: The dimensionless size factor k_b.

member.name: M:MelloSilveiraTools.MechanicsOfMaterials.Fatigue.FatigueCalculator.CalculateLoadingFactor(MelloSilveiraTools.MechanicsOfMaterials.Models.Fatigue.LoadingType)
member.summary: Calculates the Marin loading factor k_c using the standard discrete values from Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design: 1 for bending, 0.85 for axial loads and 0.59 for torsion.
member.param: The loading type applied to the part.
member.returns: The dimensionless loading factor k_c.

member.name: M:MelloSilveiraTools.MechanicsOfMaterials.Fatigue.FatigueCalculator.CalculateTemperatureFactor(System.Double)
member.summary: Calculates the Marin temperature factor k_d. The current implementation always returns 1 because the operating temperature window for Baja SAE structural analyses does not vary enough to meaningfully reduce the endurance limit. Reference: Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design.
member.param: The operating temperature of the part, in degrees Celsius. Currently unused.
member.returns: The dimensionless temperature factor k_d (always 1 in this implementation).

member.name: M:MelloSilveiraTools.MechanicsOfMaterials.Fatigue.FatigueCalculator.CalculateReliabilityFactor(MelloSilveiraTools.MechanicsOfMaterials.Models.Enums.Reliability)
member.summary: Calculates the Marin reliability factor k_e using the standard discrete values from Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design (Table 6-5): 1.000 (50%), 0.897 (90%), 0.868 (95%), 0.814 (99%), 0.753 (99.9%).
member.param: The desired reliability level for the fatigue analysis.
member.returns: The dimensionless reliability factor k_e.
